full_text_en:
Ren Da Building Materials Factory v. Xin Yi Company — patent infringement dispute

【Ruling Summary】

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 56, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the PRC, the scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the patent claims. All technical features that the patentee writes into the patent claims are essential technical features and shall be included in the comparison of technical features.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

No. 1 of (2005) Min San Ti Zi

Original Appellant: Dalian Xinyi Building Materials Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dongjiagou Street, Dalian Development Zone.

Legal Representative: Sun Changfu, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Hongyi, lawyer of Beijing Lifang Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jin, staff member of the Company.

Original Appellee: Dalian Renda New-type Wall Building Materials Factory, domiciled at No. 32 Bo'ai Street, Xigang District, Dalian City.

Legal Representative: Liu Xiping, Manager of the Factory.

Agent ad litem: Zhou Zhijian, lawyer of Dalian Wisdom Patent Office.

Agent ad litem: Qi Hang, staff member of the Factory.

In the case concerning the dispute over patent infringement between the original appellant Dalian Xinyi Building Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xinyi Company) and the original appellee Dalian Renda New-type Wall Building Materials Factory (hereinafter referred to as Renda Factory), the Liaoning High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment No. 67 (2004) Liao Min Si Zhi Zhong Zi on April 19, 2004, which has become legally effective. Believing that the judgment was erroneous, Xinyi Company applied to this Court for retrial in July 2004. On December 27, 2004, this Court, by Civil Ruling No. 27 (2004) Min San Jian Zi, decided to conduct a retrial of this case. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. The legal representative of the original appellant Xinyi Company, Sun Changfu, and its agents ad litem Jiang Hongyi and Wang Jin, as well as the agents ad litem of the original appellee Renda Factory, Zhou Zhijian and Qi Hang, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

The original trial court found: On October 13, 1999, a utility model patent entitled "Concrete Thin-Wall Cylindrical Component" was granted, with the patentee being Wang Benmiao, and the patent number ZL98231113.3.

On February 16, 2001, Renda Factory entered into a patent implementation license contract with Wang Benmiao and his authorized company, Hunan Lixin Building Materials Co., Ltd. The contract stipulated that the scope of implementation of the patent in question was Liaoning Province, the license fee was RMB 200,000, and other rights and obligations of the parties were agreed upon. On June 9, 2001, the contracting parties signed a supplementary agreement, which further stipulated that Renda Factory's implementation was "exclusive use," meaning that the patent implementation license contract signed by the parties was an exclusive license contract, and also provided that "legal issues arising from the production and operation of the patented product are unrelated to Hunan Lixin Building Materials Co., Ltd.," i.e., any problems would be handled solely by Renda Factory. The license fee was changed to RMB 100,000. Based on these two agreements, Renda Factory obtained the exclusive right to use the patent in Liaoning Province.

The content of the utility model patent claim is as follows: A concrete thin-wall cylindrical component, consisting of a tube and tube bottoms closing the openings at both ends of the tube, characterized in that the tube bottom is formed by superimposing at least two layers of glass fiber cloth, each layer of glass fiber cloth being bonded by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the two side surfaces of the tube bottom are also respectively covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material. Similarly, the tube is formed by superimposing at least two layers of glass fiber cloth tubes nested inside each other, each layer of glass fiber cloth tube being bonded by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the inner cavity surface and the outer cylindrical surface of the tube are also respectively covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material.

At the beginning of 2002, Renda Factory discovered that Xinyi Company was producing and marketing products similar to the patented product. The main technical features of the product were: the tube was formed by one layer of glass fiber cloth sandwiched between two layers of cement inorganic cementitious material, and the tube bottoms closing the two ends of the tube were also made of cement inorganic cementitious material, without any glass fiber cloth. Compared with the patent in question, the tube portion of Xinyi Company's accused infringing product had one less layer of glass fiber cloth, and the tube bottom portion had no glass fiber cloth.

Dalian Intermediate People's Court held: Renda Factory is the licensee under an exclusive patent implementation license contract in Liaoning and enjoys the exclusive right of use. According to the law, a licensee under an exclusive license contract may independently bring a lawsuit before the people's court, and the patentee has also explicitly authorized this. Therefore, Renda Factory may independently institute legal proceedings before the people's court.

Although the accused infringing product of Xinyi Company differs from the patent in question, there is no essential difference. The accused infringing product also consists of a tube and tube bottoms closing the two ends of the tube, which is the same as the preamble of the patent claim. The internal structure of the tube wall of the accused infringing product is two layers of cement inorganic cementitious material sandwiching one layer of glass fiber cloth, and the tube bottom wall does not contain a glass fiber layer. Although this differs from the literal description of the structure of the tube and tube bottom in the patent claim, the main part of the patent is the tube. By using cement layers with glass fiber cloth layers interposed, the tube wall becomes both strong and thin, increasing its internal cavity volume, thereby significantly reducing the weight of the floor slab it constitutes. In other words, increasing the cavity volume and reducing weight are mainly achieved by reducing and thinning the tube wall. The tube bottom only serves to prevent the infiltration of cement mortar, playing a secondary role. Furthermore, it shows that adding a glass fiber cloth interlayer in the tube wall achieves the functional effect of increasing strength and reducing wall thickness to increase the hollow volume. Compared with the essential technical features of the independent claim of the patent, the specific technical features of the accused infringing product are: in terms of means, both involve adding glass fiber cloth between layers of cement inorganic cementitious material; the essence is the addition of a glass fiber cloth structure between cement layers. The difference between one layer and two layers is merely quantitative, and this difference does not cause a qualitative change. Therefore, the means are basically the same. In terms of function, both the addition of glass fiber cloth layers serve the functional role of enhancing thin-wall strength, particularly increasing the thin wall's tensile strength under stress and deformation. For a thin-walled tube with plugs at both ends, stress and deformation mainly occur in the tube wall. Therefore, the function of increasing tensile strength under stress and deformation is mainly reflected in the tube wall. The tube bottoms at both ends primarily serve a sealing function and bear circumferential pressure. Adding a glass fiber layer between wall layers does not increase the compressive strength of the tube bottom. As long as a glass fiber layer is added between cement layers in the tube wall, the function of enhancing tensile strength under deformation is achieved, and the resulting function is basically the same as that of the patent. In terms of effect, both effectively reduce the weight of the tube body and the floor slab, with basically the same effect. Through the above comparison, it can be seen that a person of ordinary skill in the art can choose the number of glass fiber layers according to needs and obtain a structure that does not cause essential functional changes, without the need for creative labor, and achieve basically the same effect. Therefore, the accused infringing product is basically identical to the patent in terms of means, function, and effect, constituting infringement by equivalents. The court ruled: 1. Xinyi Company shall immediately cease the production and sale of the accused infringing product; 2. Xinyi Company shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, make a written apology to Renda Factory (if not executed within the time limit, the court will publish the judgment content in a publicly distributed newspaper in Liaoning Province, with the relevant expenses borne by Xinyi Company); 3. Xinyi Company shall, within ten days after the judgment takes effect, compensate Renda Factory for losses of RMB 100,000. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 4,010 shall be borne by Xinyi Company.

Liaoning High People's Court held that the accused infringing product and the patented product are products based on the same industry usage to improve product strength and reduce product weight. Their technical concepts are basically the same, and both consist of a tube and tube bottoms closing the two ends of the tube, which is identical to the preamble of the claim. Although there is a difference in the number of glass fiber cloth layers between the accused infringing product and the essential technical features stated in the patent claim, this difference is different from numerical limitations such as those for compounds and compositions; it is merely a substitution in quantity and does not cause an essential change in the product. The court of first instance's finding that infringement by equivalents was established was not improper. The court ruled to dismiss Xinyi Company's appeal and affirm the original judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 4,010 shall be borne by Xinyi Company.

Xinyi Company applied for retrial, alleging:

1. The original trial court erroneously interpreted the scope of protection of the patent right.

First, the original trial court, on the ground that "the tube bottom plays only a secondary role," erroneously excluded from the scope of the infringement comparison the essential technical feature stated in the independent claim of the patent: "the tube bottom is formed by superimposing at least two layers of glass fiber cloth, each layer of glass fiber cloth being bonded by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the two side surfaces of the tube bottom are also respectively covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material" (hereinafter referred to as the tube bottom wall structure). Thus, the court included within the scope of patent protection the pure concrete single-layer structure of the tube bottom without glass fiber cloth, which the patentee had already excluded from the protection scope. The claim lists the tube bottom wall structure as the first distinguishing feature, indicating that the patentee considered the tube bottom portion to be very important and indispensable for achieving the purpose and effect of the invention. The specification only describes the tube bottom as "the openings at both ends of the component's tube are also closed, thus also having a good sound insulation effect." From "also having," it can be seen that the sound insulation effect is merely the secondary function of the tube bottom, implying the tube bottom also has a primary function other than sound insulation. Since the specification does not specifically describe the primary function of the tube bottom, a person skilled in the art, upon reading the claims and specification comprehensively, can only assume that the primary function of the tube bottom is the same as that of the tube. Moreover, there is no description anywhere in the specification indicating that the tube bottom wall structure is non-essential. Therefore, the tube bottom wall structure is an essential technical feature. Furthermore, prior to the filing date of the patent, existing technology had already disclosed structures in which the tube wall was made of three cement layers with two layers of glass fiber cloth sandwiched in between, i.e., five or more layers. Consequently, the only feature distinguishing the patent from the prior art is actually the tube bottom wall structure. The "doctrine of non-essential elements" should not be applied to ignore the tube bottom wall structure in this case. Second, the original trial court erroneously, on the ground that "one layer versus two layers is merely a difference in quantity that does not cause a qualitative change," re-included within the scope of patent protection the technical solution in which the tube wall contains only one layer of glass fiber cloth, a solution clearly excluded by the patentee. In fact, the patent claim explicitly uses the limitation "at least two layers" rather than "two layers," a clear boundary and baseline to limit the number of glass fiber cloth layers in the wall. This indicates that the patentee considered that the number of glass fiber cloth layers in the wall cannot be less than two, otherwise, the purpose of the invention could not be achieved or the patent could not be distinguished from the prior art. Therefore, the patentee used the limiting feature "at least two layers" to exclude technical solutions that do not use or use only one layer of glass fiber cloth from the scope of patent protection. The original trial court clearly deviated from the patentee's intent and the quantitative limitation set forth in the independent claim, improperly expanding the patent's protection scope and harming public interests.

2. The original trial court erroneously applied the principle of determining infringement by equivalents.

Pursuant to the relevant judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court, equivalence refers to equivalence of individual technical features, not equivalence of the overall technical solution. Compared with the patent, the accused infringing product has at least two fewer layers of cement and one fewer layer of glass fiber cloth in the tube wall portion, and at least two fewer layers of cement and two fewer layers of glass fiber cloth in the tube bottom wall portion, showing a clear structural difference. However, the original trial court, on the ground that "the defendant's product is basically the same as the patent in terms of means, function, and effect," found that the defendant's product constituted equivalence with the patent, clearly violating the Supreme People's Court's provisions on equivalence determination. As for Renda Factory's claim that technological progress allows the use of only one layer of glass fiber cloth to achieve the patent's purpose, Xinyi Company has provided evidence proving that alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth was already applied in China before the patent filing date. Moreover, the patent in question is a utility model patent, which protects features of product shape, structure, or combination, and does not involve material features. Therefore, Renda Factory's argument that equivalence arose from technological progress in glass fiber cloth is untenable.

3. The original trial court's order to apologize lacks legal basis.

A patent right is primarily a property right and does not involve personal rights. Therefore, the Patent Law does not provide for the application of a civil liability method such as an apology, which targets personal rights, in handling patent infringement disputes. The original trial court's order requiring Xinyi Company to apologize is legally unfounded.

In summary, Xinyi Company believes that the original judgment contains clear errors and requests this Court to: set aside Civil Judgment No. 67 (2004) Liao Min Si Zhi Zhong Zi; dismiss all claims of Renda Factory; order Renda Factory to publish the retrial judgment in "Dalian Daily"; and have Renda Factory bear all litigation costs for the first and second instances.

Renda Factory responded:

1. According to the description in the patent specification, the main part of the concrete thin-wall cylindrical component, the tube wall, uses cement layers with glass fiber cloth layers sandwiched in between, making the tube wall both strong and thin, correspondingly increasing the internal cavity volume by multiples, thereby significantly reducing the weight of the floor slab it constitutes. It can be seen that achieving the invention's purpose of increasing cavity volume and reducing weight is mainly accomplished by reducing and thinning the tube wall, while reducing and thinning the tube bottom has no effect. The function of increasing the thin wall's tensile strength under stress is primarily in the tube wall. Adding one or two layers of glass fiber cloth in the tube wall serves the functional role of enhancing tensile strength. The tube bottom primarily serves a sealing function; adding a glass fiber layer between wall layers does not increase the radial compressive strength of the tube bottom. Therefore, the tube bottom wall structure is not an essential technical feature of the patent.

2. The technical features of the tube portion of the accused infringing product are equivalent to the corresponding technical features of the patent. This is because: both adopt the means of adding a glass fiber cloth layer between cement layers; the difference between one layer and two layers of glass fiber cloth is quantitative, not qualitative, so the means are basically the same; both the addition of glass fiber cloth layers serve to enhance thin-wall strength. Stress and deformation mainly occur in the tube wall; as long as a glass fiber layer is added between cement layers in the tube wall, the function of increasing strength is achieved; the effect of both is to effectively increase the internal cavity volume of the tube body, reduce tube wall thickness, and floor slab weight. Moreover, the selection of the number of glass fiber cloth layers can be conceived without the need for creative labor.

Furthermore, with advances in glass fiber cloth technology, after the patent application, using a single layer of glass fiber cloth can achieve the patent's purpose. At the time of the patent application, only standards for non-alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth existed. It was only after the issuance of the standard for alkali-resistant glass fiber mesh in 1999 that formal alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth came into use. Alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth has good corrosion resistance, so using a single layer of glass fiber cloth in the tube wall can produce a good tube component product, achieving functions and effects basically the same as the patent. The phrase "at least two layers of glass fiber cloth" in the patent claim represents the best technical solution. The glass fiber cloth in the tube bottom can be included or omitted, but when the cement pressure is high, glass fiber cloth can be sandwiched in the tube bottom, allowing the tube bottom to be made thinner, reducing weight, and making the tube body less prone to bending. Additionally, whether the tube joint portions of the accused infringing product overlap does not affect the determination of equivalence.

3. The prior art solution cited by Xinyi Company is not a closed tube body used to fill cast-in-place floor slabs and is not under the same subject matter as the patent solution. Therefore, Xinyi Company's argument that the tube bottom wall structure is the sole distinguishing feature of the patent cannot stand.

4. Apology is one of the civil liability methods provided by law. Xinyi Company's intentional infringement will inevitably cause adverse effects on the patentee's reputation among its peers, and requiring an apology is not excessive.

Within the time limit for presenting evidence, Renda Factory submitted new evidence to this Court: 1. The industry standard for glass fiber mesh implemented in 1995; 2. The industry standard for alkali-resistant glass fiber mesh implemented in 1999; 3. A testimony issued by Tangshan Hengtai Glass Fiber Products Co., Ltd. This evidence is intended to show that, with advances in glass fiber cloth technology, the number of glass fiber cloth layers can be reduced to one while still achieving the effect of the patent. Since the accused infringing product uses one layer of glass fiber cloth in the tube wall, it also constitutes infringement. In response, Xinyi Company submitted counter-evidence: 1. The article "Alkali-Resistant Glass Fiber Coated Mesh" published in the first issue of "Beijing Building Materials" in 1996; 2. The industry standard for glass fiber reinforced cement corrugated sheets and ridge tiles implemented in 1995. This evidence is intended to show that, before the patent filing date, alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth was already applied as existing technology. Additionally, during the trial, Renda Factory also admitted that alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth existed domestically before the filing date, although there was no industry standard.

Upon investigation, this Court finds that the facts found by the original trial court are basically true.

It is further found that alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth existed before the patent filing date.

This Court holds: In light of the facts and reasons alleged by Xinyi Company in its retrial application and Renda Factory's response, the following three issues are mainly involved in this case:

I. Whether the tube bottom wall structure is an essential technical feature of the patent.

First, from the perspective of the drafting requirements for patent claims, Article 20 and Article 21 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the PRC clearly provide that the claims shall clearly and concisely define the scope of protection sought. The claims shall contain an independent claim. The independent claim shall reflect the technical solution of the invention or utility model as a whole and shall state the essential technical features necessary for solving the technical problem. It should be considered that all technical features stated by the patentee in the independent claim are essential technical features and shall not be ignored, and all shall be included in the comparison of technical features. This Court does not approve of the careless application of the so-called "doctrine of surplus designation." Second, from the perspective of the function of the claims, according to the provisions of Article 56, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the PRC, the scope of protection of the invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The function of the claims is to define the scope of patent protection. That is, by indicating to the public all the technical features constituting the technical solution of the invention or utility model, the public can clearly know what acts would infringe the patent right, thereby providing effective and reasonable protection for the patentee on the one hand, and ensuring the public's freedom to use the technology on the other hand. Only by giving full and complete respect to all the technical features recorded in the claims will the public not be at a loss due to unpredictable changes in the content of the claims, thereby ensuring the certainty of legal rights and fundamentally guaranteeing the normal operation and value realization of the patent system. The patent claims in this case contain only one claim, namely the independent claim. This independent claim clearly records the wall layer structures of the cylinder bottom and the cylinder tube respectively. Therefore, the assertion of Renda Factory that the cylinder bottom wall layer structure of the patent is not an essential technical feature cannot be established. "The cylinder bottom is formed by laminating at least two layers of glass fiber cloth, the layers of glass fiber cloth being bonded together by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the two side surfaces of the cylinder bottom are also each covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material" is an essential technical feature of the patent in this case.

Accordingly, all the essential technical features of the patent in this case are: (1) the cylinder tube; (2) the cylinder bottom sealing the two end openings of the cylinder tube; (3) the cylinder bottom is formed by laminating at least two layers of glass fiber cloth, the layers of glass fiber cloth being bonded together by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the two side surfaces of the cylinder bottom are also each covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material; (4) the cylinder tube is formed by sleeving at least two layers of glass fiber cloth tubes, the layers of glass fiber cloth tubes being bonded together by a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material, and the inner cavity surface and the outer cylindrical surface of the cylinder tube are also each covered with a layer of sulfoaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material or ferroaluminate cement inorganic cementitious material.

Compared with this essential technical feature of the cylinder bottom wall layer structure of the patent, the cylinder bottom of the allegedly infringing product contains no glass fiber cloth in the cement inorganic cementitious material. Obviously, they are not identical. Furthermore, because the cement inorganic cementitious material of the cylinder bottom of the allegedly infringing product does not contain glass fiber cloth interlayered, while the cement inorganic cementitious material of the patented cylinder bottom has at least two layers of glass fiber cloth interlayered at intervals, they do not belong to substantially the same means, and therefore are not equivalent either. The mere fact that the technical feature of the cylinder bottom of the allegedly infringing product is neither identical nor equivalent to the corresponding technical feature of the patent is sufficient to determine that the allegedly infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent.

2. Whether the feature of the cylinder tube portion of the allegedly infringing product having a layer of glass fiber cloth interlayered in the cement inorganic cementitious material constitutes an equivalent feature to the corresponding technical feature of the patent.

First, according to the provisions of Article 56, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the PRC, the scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent is determined by the content of the claims, and the description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims. Since the claims of the patent in this case, when describing the number of layers of glass fiber cloth, clearly use the limiting term "at least two layers" which has a very clear boundary, and the description also clearly states that the number of sleeved layers of glass fiber cloth tubes "can be as few as only two layers," this clear limitation should not be violated when interpreting the claims. It should be considered that a person of ordinary skill in the art, upon reading the claims and the description, would not conceive that the object of the invention could still be achieved by containing only one layer of glass fiber cloth or no glass fiber cloth at all. Therefore, structures containing only one layer of glass fiber cloth or no glass fiber cloth should be excluded from the scope of patent protection. Otherwise, it would be equivalent to deleting "at least two layers" from the independent claim, leading to an unreasonable expansion of the scope of patent protection and harming the interests of the public. Second, in the patent of this case, the difference in the number of layers of glass fiber cloth cannot be simply regarded as a mere quantitative difference; rather, it has different functions in terms of physical mechanics regarding the compressive strength of the cylinder member, the volume of the inner cavity, and the weight of the floor. The cylinder tube portion containing "at least two layers" of glass fiber cloth achieves technical effects in enhancing compressive strength, reducing floor weight, and increasing inner cavity volume that are superior to those achieved by the cylinder tube portion containing only "one layer" of glass fiber cloth. It should be considered that containing only "one layer" of glass fiber cloth cannot achieve substantially the same effects as containing "at least two layers" of glass fiber cloth. Therefore, the feature of the cylinder tube portion of the allegedly infringing product having a layer of glass fiber cloth interlayered in the cement inorganic cementitious material does not constitute a feature equivalent to the corresponding technical feature of the patent, and is certainly not an identical feature. Consequently, the allegedly infringing product also does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent.

Furthermore, regarding the issue of alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth, since alkali-resistant glass fiber cloth existed before the patent application date, the patent applicant should have foreseen this, yet still used the wording "at least two layers of glass fiber cloth" in the claims. Therefore, the assertion of Renda Factory that technological progress in glass fiber cloth leads to a finding of equivalent infringement cannot be established. Regarding the issue of the seam of the cylinder tube of the allegedly infringing product, since Renda Factory admitted that whether or not the seams of the cylinder tube of the allegedly infringing product overlap does not affect the determination of equivalence, this Court will not comment further on this.

3. Whether the form of liability of making an apology is applicable in this case.

Making an apology is primarily a form of liability directed at damage to personal interests and commercial reputation. Patent rights are mainly a property interest, so making an apology is generally not applicable in patent infringement dispute cases. Since the court of first instance, without evidence proving that the actions of Xinyi Company caused significant damage to the commercial reputation of Renda Factory, ordered Xinyi Company to make an apology, this was inappropriate. However, because Xinyi Company did not provide corresponding evidence during the retrial to prove that the original judgment had been published and the adverse impact it had on Xinyi Company, this Court finds it difficult to support Xinyi Company's retrial request regarding the publication of the retrial judgment to remedy the impact of the publication of the original judgment.

In summary, the cylinder bottom of the allegedly infringing product contains no glass fiber cloth in the cement inorganic cementitious material, and compared with the cylinder bottom wall layer structure of the patent, it is neither an identical feature nor an equivalent feature; the feature of the cylinder tube portion of the allegedly infringing product of "a layer of glass fiber cloth interlayered in the cement material" cannot achieve substantially the same effect as the feature of the patented cylinder tube portion of "at least two layers of glass fiber cloth interlayered at intervals in the cement material." The technical features of the cylinder tube portion of the allegedly infringing product do not constitute equivalent features, and certainly not identical features, to the corresponding technical features of the patent. Therefore, the allegedly infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent, and the actions of Xinyi Company do not constitute infringement of the patent in question. The judgment of the court of first instance, on the grounds that the main part of the patent is the cylinder tube and the cylinder bottom plays a secondary role, ignored the essential technical feature of the cylinder bottom wall layer structure clearly recorded in the claims and did not include it in the comparison of technical features. Furthermore, in understanding "one layer" versus "at least two layers" of glass fiber cloth in the cylinder tube portion, it erroneously considered it a mere quantitative difference, thereby finding that the constituent elements of equivalent features were met and that equivalent infringement was established. This constitutes an error in the application of law and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 56, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law of the PRC, Article 21, paragraph 2 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the PRC, Article 17 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Dispute Cases, and Article 177, paragraph 2 and Article 184, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2004) Liao Min Si Zhi Zhong Zi No. 67 of the Liaoning High People's Court is reversed;

2. The claims of Dalian Renda New Wall Building Materials Factory are dismissed. The total case acceptance fee for the first instance and second instance is RMB 8,020, to be borne by Dalian Renda New Wall Building Materials Factory.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Yongchang

Acting Judge: Xi Zhonglin

Acting Judge: Li Jian

August 22, 2005
